commands.author: zhangqueping

target.title: fix: skip pushLoopFailure for MidTurnPrecheckSignal control-flow errors
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` — a control-flow signal thrown in `transformContext` to trigger tool-result truncation — was caught by `Agent.handleRunFailure` which unconditionally pushed a synthetic failure into the event stream, causing users to see a premature "Context overflow" error even though the internal retry succeeds.

**Solution**: Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with a `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel so `Agent.handleRunFailure` can recognize control-flow signals, skip the synthetic failure push, and instead emit a clean `agent_end` event to settle lifecycle subscribers (compaction waiters, session-state cleanup, terminal hooks). The existing attempt-runner recovery path (via `pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest` callback) handles truncation and retry correctly.

**What changed**: `agent.ts` (`handleRunFailure`): For control-flow errors, skip synthetic failure push but still emit clean `agent_end` with actual state messages so lifecycle subscribers settle properly. Added `isControlFlowError()` helper and `AGENT_CORE_CONTROL_FLOW_SENTINEL` constant with JSDoc contract. `midturn-precheck.ts`: Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with sentinel. `agent-loop.test.ts`: Added 2 Agent-level tests verifying clean `agent_end` for control-flow signals and error events for real errors.

**What did NOT change**: `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API (unchanged — fix scoped to `Agent` class production path). `attempt.ts` recovery logic. `run.ts` retry logic. `tool-result-context-guard.ts` signal throw.

Fixes #101621

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool result makes the next prompt exceed the context budget during a tool loop, `transformContext` throws `MidTurnPrecheckSignal`. This signal is a **control-flow mechanism**, not a terminal error. The throw interrupts the tool loop before the next LLM call, and the attempt runner handles truncation + retry via a side-channel callback (`pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest`).

However, `Agent.handleRunFailure` was treating this signal as a real error and pushing a synthetic failure with `isError=true` and `"Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (mid-turn precheck)"` into the event stream. The user sees this error immediately, even though ~15 seconds later the retry succeeds silently.

## Root Cause

The production call path: `transformContext() throws MidTurnPrecheckSignal → streamAssistantResponse() → runLoop() → runAgentLoop() → Agent.runPromptMessages() → Agent.runWithLifecycle() catch → handleRunFailure(error)` pushes synthetic error. `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` extends `Error` and was indistinguishable from real errors at the agent-core layer.

## Design decisions

**Why agent-core sentinel vs embedded-runner-owned fix**: The sentinel uses `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` — owned by the agent-core package, not OpenClaw-specific. This makes the contract explicit and documented. The `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API is not used in production — the production path goes through the `Agent` class → `runAgentLoop` (async).

**Why clean agent_end instead of silent return**: The first iteration returned silently, but ClawSweeper correctly noted this could leave lifecycle subscribers in an inconsistent state. The fix now emits `agent_end` with the current state messages so compaction waiters, session-state cleanup, and terminal hooks still see the run end, while no error event leaks.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `Agent.handleRunFailure` emits a clean `agent_end` (no error event) for control-flow signals, while still emitting error events for real errors

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 24.13.1

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
npx tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json proof-script.mjs
pnpm test -- packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts
pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-context-guard.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
================================================================
PR #101648 — Real Behavior Proof (Round 3)
Node: v24.13.1

Check 0: MidTurnPrecheckSignal carries sentinel → ✅ PASS
Proof 1: Control-flow → clean agent_end, no error event → ✅ PASS
  Error events (expect 0): 0 | agent_end events (expect 1): 1
Proof 2: Real error → error + agent_end → ✅ PASS
  Error events (expect 1): 1 | agent_end events (expect 1): 1
Proof 3: Plain Error → error + agent_end → ✅ PASS
  Error events (expect 1): 1 | agent_end events (expect 1): 1

VERDICT: ✅ ALL 7 CHECKS PASSED
```

Unit tests: 24/24 (agent-loop) + 90/90 (lifecycle + tool-result-context-guard) = 114/114 passed.

**Observed result after the fix**: Control-flow signals produce clean `agent_end` (lifecycle subscribers settle) with no error event. Real errors still produce error event + `agent_end`. All lifecycle and tool-result-context-guard tests pass.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end large-MCP-output scenario requiring a configured LLM provider with API keys, not available in the current CI environment. The proof exercises the exact error propagation path with real production objects.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low risk — only errors carrying `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel are handled specially, currently only `MidTurnPrecheckSignal`
- [x] Control-flow signals now emit `agent_end` (lifecycle settlement) instead of returning silently — addressed review concern
- [x] Real errors (without sentinel) still trigger full error handling — 2 regression tests confirm
- [x] The sentinel name is owned by agent-core package, explicit JSDoc contract
- [x] Lifecycle subscribers, compaction waiters, and terminal hooks all see clean `agent_end`
- [x] No breaking API changes, no new dependencies
- [x] 114/114 tests pass including lifecycle + tool-result-context-guard suites
